tags.name: Vertigo
tags.marine_life: grey reef sharks and blacktip reef sharks (10-40 per dive), whitetip reef sharks, groupers, snappers, moray eels, Napoleon wrasse
tags.notes: Re-audited 2026-08-13. SOURCE CONFLICT FOUND: mantaray.com's general site-index page (mantaray.com/sites/vertigo/) now describes Vertigo as a shallow 10-20m reef wall with gentle-to-no current and does not mention shark feeding. This directly conflicts with mantaray.com's own dedicated shark-diving page (mantaray.com/vertigo-shark-diving/), DAN Alert Diver, ikelite.com, and a ScubaBoard trip report (630298), all four of which independently confirm a 25+ year baited shark dive on a wall with moderate-to-strong current, 10-40 grey reef/blacktip sharks, and depths well beyond the shallow reef plateau. Given 4 independent/quasi-independent confirmations vs. 1 outlying page, the wall/feeding profile is treated as accurate; the conflict is documented in the markdown per anti-hallucination policy rather than silently resolved. visityap.com no longer used as source -- it only describes sharks circling, does not add depth/current/feeding detail beyond what's already covered.

tags.history: WWII Japanese aircraft, bullet holes visible in wings; identity of THIS underwater wreck unconfirmed
tags.notes: Re-audited 2026-08-13. CORRECTION: visityap.com does NOT mention this wreck at all (checked directly) -- removed as a false source citation from prior QA pass. WRECK-HISTORY CROSS-CHECK: this underwater wreck (3-10m, near Vertigo) is distinct from the LAND-based Japanese Zero fighter wrecks near Yap's old airfield, which tracesofwar.com and traveladventures.org identify with more confidence (as an A6M5B / A6M5 Zero variant, destroyed by US forces while taxiing, wrecks now rusting in the grass). Those land-wreck sources do NOT describe the diveable underwater wreck and should not be read as confirming its identity. mantaray.com (the only source that actually discusses the underwater wreck) remains uncertain between Zero and Betty. No third source describing the underwater wreck specifically could be found this pass -- identity uncertainty is preserved rather than resolved by analogy to the (different) land wrecks.

Re-audited 2026-08-13, still unresolved. No reliable independent source confirms 'Manta Ray Bay' as a named dive site distinct from the resort. One low-quality aggregator (techdivetravels.com) lists a 'Manta Ray Bay' site, but that source is judged unreliable on this pass (see Gilman Wall note) and is not counted. Confirmed named manta sites remain: Mi'l Channel cleaning stations + Tzimoulis Ridge (northwest), and Stammtisch / Valley of the Rays (Goofnuw Channel, northeast) -- none of which is called 'Manta Ray Bay'. Marked unresolved.

tags.notes: MAJOR CORRECTION (2026-08-13): the pre-existing markdown for 'Land's End' described strong/unpredictable current, hammerhead sharks, and yellowfin/dogtooth tuna hunting baitfish at a current-convergence point -- NONE of this is corroborated by any source and it directly CONTRADICTS the two sources that do describe the likely-matching site. mantaray.com's dedicated 'End of the Land' page and visityap.com both independently describe a near-vertical wall (18-40m) with MINIMAL current (0-3km/h) and RESTING (not hunting) sharks plus black-spotted stingrays and turtles -- essentially the opposite current/pelagic-action profile from what was previously written. This is very likely the same site under a slightly different name/word-order, but because the name doesn't match exactly and only 2 domains were found, validated remains false pending a third source or exact-name confirmation. Data and description corrected to match the 2 real sources; the fabricated pelagic-action content has been removed as a hallucination.
